full_judgment: 2. It is stated in the writ petition that one Syed' Abdul Waheed acquired ownership in the aforesaid holding No. 10.3, Block-B, Iqubal Road, Dhaka by virtue of 99 years lease vide lease deed No. 16348 dated 30.12.1963 by the Government of the then East Pakistan. While said Syed Abdul Waheed had been residing with his family in the house on the said holding he executed a registered deed of Power of Attorney dated 21.8.72 in favour of Paster David Paul Rema, Secretary of Bangladesh Section of Seventh Day Adventists, a Christan Missionary organization situated at Mirpur, Dhaka authorizing him to look after and sell the said house property as he had to go abroad and he had no other relation in Bangladesh to look after and sell the same. Said Paster David Paul Rema as the constituted Attorney of Syed Abdul Waheed while in occupation and possession of the said house sold the same to Lawrence Bennett under five registered sale deed. Nos. 2880 dated 29.6.1979, 2884 dated 30.6.1979, 2895 dated 2.7.1999, 2896 dated 2.7.1979 and 3209 dated 20.7.1979. Meanwhile, possession of the said house was forcibly taken over from Pasteur David Paul in 1975 by some miscreants with the help of corrupt government officials and the government then enlisted the said house as an abandoned property towards the end of 1975. Accordingly, said Paster David Paul Rema and Lowrance Benett in Iurn submitted applications with the Ministry of Works for release of the said house without any success. Thereafter said Lowrance Benett being in need of money sold the said house property to the petitioner, Mrs. Shahida Begum by a registered sale deed No. 1980 dated 20.9.87 and handed over all the basic documents of title to him in original. After the purchase the petitioner came to know that the said house was already included in the "Ka" list as an abandoned building vide serial No. 21, Page 9762(15) of the gazette dated 23.9.1986. The petitioner then filed an application under section 7 of the said Ordinance 1985 for release of the said house by excluding the same from the "Ka' list of the said gazette. But the Court of Settlement refused to entertain the application on the ground of limitation. Against this backdrop, the petitioner filed the writ petition and obtained the present Rule.
